nodes.raw_latex:
Condition \eqref{eq:mainthmcondition2} is very natural: it requires the rate of (combinations of) mergers involving three or more lineages to be vanishingly small in comparison to that of binary mergers.
The sequence $( b_N )_{ N \in \mathbb{N} }$ controls the rate at which the ratio of rates of large and binary mergers vanishes, and can decay to zero arbitrarily slowly.
The exact values of its entries are not special; it is just the sequence that plays an implicit role in the usual little-o notation.
As mentioned in Section \ref{sec:intro}, a natural analogue of \eqref{eq:mainthmcondition2} is known to be necessary and sufficient for convergence to the $n$-coalescent in the neutral case \citep[Equation (16)]{mohle2000}.

nodes.statement: The structure of the proof follows citetmohle1999, albeit with considerable technical complication due to the dependence between generations (non-neutrality) in our model. To make it digestible, the proof is broken down into a number of results which are organised into sections; the relationships between these are shown in Figure~. The structure of the proof follows \citet{mohle1999}, albeit with considerable technical complication due to the dependence between generations (non-neutrality) in our model.
To make it digestible, the proof is broken down into a number of results which are organised into sections; the relationships between these are shown in Figure~\ref{fig:weakconv_structure}.

Convergence of the finite-dimensional distributions was proved in \citet[Theorem 3.2]{brown2021}.
Strengthening this to weak convergence on the space of processes amounts to establishing relative compactness of the sequence $\{ (G_{\tau_N(t)}^{(n,N)})_{t\geq0} \}_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$.
Since $\mathcal{P}_n$ is finite and therefore complete and separable, and the sample paths of $(G_{\tau_N(t)}^{(n,N)})_{t\geq0}$ live in $\mathcal{D}$, we can apply \citet[Chapter 3, Corollary 7.4]{ethier1986} which states that a sequence of processes $\{ (G_{\tau_N(t)}^{(n,N)})_{t\geq0} \}_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ is relatively compact if and only if the following two conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \label{item:relcomp1} For every $\epsilon>0$ and rational $t\geq 0$, there exists a compact set $\Gamma_{ \epsilon, t } \subseteq \mathcal{P}_n$ such that
\begin{equation*}
\liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ G_{\tau_N(t)}^{(n,N)} \in \Gamma_{ \epsilon, t } \right] 
\geq 1-\epsilon.
\end{equation*}
\item \label{item:relcomp2} For every $\epsilon>0$, $t>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{modulus_of_continuity}
\liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \omega\left( G_{\tau_N(\cdot)}^{(n,N)}, \delta, t \right) < \epsilon \right] 
\geq 1-\epsilon,
\end{equation}
where $\omega$ is the modified modulus of continuity:
\begin{equation*}
\omega\left( G_{\tau_N(\cdot)}^{(n,N)}, \delta, t \right) := \inf \max_{i \in [K]} 
        \sup_{u,v \in [T_{i-1}, T_i)} \rho\left( 
        G_{\tau_N(u)}^{(n,N)}, G_{\tau_N(v)}^{(n,N)} \right),
\end{equation*}
with the infimum taken over all partitions of the form $0=T_0<T_1<\cdots <T_{K-1} <t \leq T_K$ (for any $K$) such that $\min_{i\in[K]} (T_i - T_{i-1}) > \delta$. 
\end{enumerate}
Since $\mathcal{P}_n$ is finite and hence compact, Condition~\ref{item:relcomp1} is satisfied automatically with $\Gamma_{ \epsilon, t } = \mathcal{P}_n$. 
Intuitively, Condition~\ref{item:relcomp2} ensures that the jumps of the process are well-separated. 
In our case, $\rho( G_{\tau_N(u)}^{(n,N)}, G_{\tau_N(v)}^{(n,N)} ) = 1$ if there is at least one jump between times $u$ and $v$, and 0 otherwise.
The supremum and maximum indicate whether there is a jump inside any of the intervals of the given partition; this can be zero only if all of the jumps up to time $t$ occur exactly at the times $T_{ 0 : K }$. 
The infimum over all allowed partitions can only equal zero if no two jumps occur less than $\delta$ (unscaled) time apart.

To prove Theorem \ref{thm:weakconv}, it remains to verify Condition \ref{item:relcomp2}.
To do this, we use a coupling with a process for which Condition \ref{item:relcomp2} is easier to check, and which will imply that it also holds for the genealogical process of interest.
Define $p_t := \max_{\xi\in \mathcal{P}_n} \{1 - p_{\xi\xi}(t)\} = 1 - p_{\Delta\Delta}(t)$, where $\Delta = \{ \{1\},\dots, \{n\} \}$.
For a proof that the maximum is attained at $\xi = \Delta$, see Lemma~\ref{thm:maximum_pr}. 
Following \citet{mohle1999}, we construct the process $(Z_t, S_t)_{t \in \mathbb{N}_0}$ on $\mathbb{N}_0 \times \mathcal{P}_n$ with initial state $( Z_0, S_0 ) = ( 0, \Delta )$, and conditional transition probabilities
\begin{align}
\mathbb{P}[ Z_t = j , S_t = \eta \mid& Z_{t-1} = i, S_{t-1} = \xi, \mathcal{F}_\infty ] \notag\\
&= \begin{cases}
1 - p_t &\quad \text{if } j=i \text{ and } \eta=\xi, \\
p_{\xi\xi}(t) + p_t - 1  &\quad \text{if } j=i+1 \text{ and } \eta=\xi, \\
p_{\xi\eta}(t) &\quad \text{if } j=i+1 \text{ and } \eta\neq\xi, \\
0 &\quad \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\label{eq:constructed_chain}
\end{align}
The definition of $p_t$ ensures that the second case of \eqref{eq:constructed_chain} is non-negative, attaining the value zero when $\xi=\Delta$.

Unlike the corresponding process in \citet{mohle1999}, the transition probabilities in \eqref{eq:constructed_chain} depend on offspring counts. Thus, $(Z_t, S_t)$ is only Markovian conditional on $\mathcal{F}_\infty$, and can be thought of as a time-inhomogeneous Markov chain in a random environment.
Marginally, $(S_t)$ has the same distribution as the genealogical process of interest, while $(Z_t)$ jumps whenever $(S_t)$ does, but also has some extra jumps.
The jump times of $(Z_t)$ do not depend on the current state, making it much easier to analyse.
Our construction also resembles that of \citet{mohle2002coal}, where the process $(S_t)$ is also time-inhomogeneous but still Markovian without conditioning on a random environment.

The coupling of jumps implies that the modulus of continuity of $(Z_t)$ is at least as large as that of $(S_t)$.
Hence, we will show that \eqref{modulus_of_continuity} holds for $(Z_t)$, and conclude that it also holds for the genealogical processes of interest.
Denote by $0=T_0^{(N)}<T_1^{(N)}<\dots$ the jump times of the rescaled process $(Z_{\tau_N(t)})_{t\geq0}$, and by $\varpi_i^{(N)} := T_i^{(N)} - T_{i-1}^{(N)}$ the corresponding holding times.
Suppose that for some fixed $\varpi_1^{(N)}, \varpi_2^{(N)}, \dots$ and $t>0$, there exists $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\delta >0$ such that
$\varpi_i^{(N)} > \delta$ for all $i\in [m]$, and
$T_m^{(N)} \geq t$.
Then
$K_N := \min\{i : T_i^{(N)} \geq t\}$
is well-defined with $1\leq K_N \leq m$,
and $T_{ 1 : K_N }^{(N)}$ is a partition of the form required for Condition~\ref{item:relcomp2}.
Indeed $(Z_{\tau_N(\cdot)})$ is constant on every interval $[ T_{i-1}^{(N)} , T_i^{(N)} )$ by construction, so $\omega( (Z_{\tau_N(\cdot))} , \delta, t ) = 0$. 
We therefore have that
for each $m \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\delta >0$,
\begin{equation*}
\mathbb{P}\left[ \omega\left( (Z_{\tau_N(\cdot)}) , \delta, t \right) < \epsilon \right]
\geq \mathbb{P}\left[ T_m^{(N)} \geq t, \varpi_i^{(N)} > \delta \,\forall i\in [m] \right] .
\end{equation*}
Thus, a sufficient condition for Condition~\ref{item:relcomp2} to hold is: 
for any $\epsilon>0$, $t>0$, there exist $m\in\mathbb{N}$, $\delta>0$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:condition2b}
\liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_m^{(N)} \geq t, \varpi_i^{(N)} > \delta \,\forall i\in [m]\right]
\geq 1-\epsilon .
\end{equation}
By Lemma~\ref{thm:holdingtimes_distn}, below, the limiting distributions of $\varpi_i^{(N)}$ are i.i.d.\ $\operatorname{Exp}(\alpha_n)$, where $\alpha_n := n(n-1)/2$, so
\begin{equation*}
\limsup_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \varpi_i^{(N)} \leq \delta \right] 
= 1- \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \varpi_i^{(N)} > \delta \right] 
= 1- e^{-\alpha_n \delta}
\end{equation*}
for each $i$, and
\begin{align*}
\limsup_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_m^{(N)} < t \right]
&= 1- \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_m^{(N)} \geq t \right] \\
&= 1- \liminf_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \varpi_1^{(N)} + \cdots + \varpi_m^{(N)} \geq t \right] \\
&= 1- e^{-\alpha_n t} \sum_{i=0}^{m-1} \frac{(\alpha_n t)^i}{i!},
\end{align*}
using the series expansion for the Erlang CDF \citep[see for example][Chapter 15]{forbes2011}.
Now
\begin{align*}
\liminf_{N\to\infty} 
        \mathbb{P}[ T_m^{(N)} \geq t, &\varpi_i^{(N)} > \delta 
        \,\forall i\in [m] ] \\
&\geq 1 - \limsup_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ T_m^{(N)} < t \right] 
        - \sum_{i=1}^m \limsup_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \varpi_i^{(N)} \leq \delta\right]\\
&= 1- \Bigg( 1- e^{-\alpha_n t} \sum_{i=0}^{m-1} 
        \frac{(\alpha_n t)^i}{i!} \Bigg) - m( 1- e^{-\alpha_n \delta} ) ,
\end{align*}
which can be made $\geq 1-\epsilon$ by taking $m$ sufficiently large and $\delta$ sufficiently small.
Since this argument applies for any $\epsilon$ and $t$, \eqref{eq:condition2b} is satisfied.
Hence, so is Condition~\ref{item:relcomp2}, and the proof is complete.

nodes.statement: For any k in N, there is a continuous bijection between the jump times T_ 1 : k ^(N) and the holding times varpi_ 1 : k ^(N). Thus, convergence of varpi_ 1 : k ^(N) to varpi_ 1 : k is equivalent to convergence of the jump times to T_ 1 : k , where T_i := varpi_1+dots+varpi_i. We will work with the jump times, following citet[Lemma 3.2]mohle1999. The idea is to prove by induction that, for any kinN and t_ 1 : k > 0, lim_Ntoinfty Pleft[ T_ 1 : k ^(N) leq t_ 1 : k right] = P[ T_ 1 : k leq t_ 1 : k ] . Take the basis case k=1, for which P[ T_1 leq t ] = P[ varpi_1 leq t ] = 1 - e^-alpha_n t and T_1^(N) >t if and only if ( Z_ tau_N( t ) ) has no jumps up to time t: Pleft[T_1^(N) >t right] = Eleft[ P[ T_1^(N) >t mid F_infty ] right] = EBigg[ prod_r=1^tau_N(t) (1-p_r) Bigg] . Lemma~ shows that this probability converges to e^-alpha_n t as required. For the induction step, assume that holds for some k. We have Pleft[ T_ 1 : ( k + 1 ) ^(N) leq t_ 1 : ( k + 1 ) right] = Pleft[ T_ 1 : k ^(N) leq t_ 1 : k right] - Pleft[ T_ 1 : k ^(N) leq t_ 1 : k , T_k+1^(N) > t_k+1 right]. The first term on the right-hand side converges to P[ T_ 1 : k leq t_ 1 : k ] by the induction hypothesis, and it remains to show that lim_Ntoinfty &Pleft[ T_ 1 : k ^(N) leq t_ 1 : k , T_k+1^(N) > t_k+1 right] = P[ T_ 1 : k leq t_ 1 : k , T_k+1 > t_k+1 ]. As shown in citet[p.\ 459]mohle1999, P[ T_ 1 : k leq t_ 1 : k , T_k+1 > t_k+1 ] = alpha_n^k e^-alpha_n t sum_substacki_1leq dotsleq i_k-1\\ in \0,dots,k\ : \\ i_j geq j forall j prod_j=1^k frac(t_j - t_j-1)^i_j - i_j-1(i_j - i_j-1)! , while the probability on the left-hand side of can be written Pleft[ T_ 1 : k ^(N) leq t_ 1 : k , T_k+1^(N) > t_k+1 right] &= Eleft[ P[ T_ 1 : k ^(N) leq t_ 1 : k , T_k+1^(N) > t_k+1 mid F_infty] right] \\ &= E Bigg[ sum_substackr_1 <dots< r_k : \\ r_i leq tau_N(t_i) forall i Big( prod_i=1^k p_r_i Big) Bigg( prod_substackr=1 \\ notin \r_1,dots,r_k\ ^tau_N(t) (1-p_r) Bigg) Bigg] . That is, there are jumps at some times r_ 1 : k , and identity transitions at all other times. A similar expression is derived in citetmohle1999, but here we have an additional expectation because the probabilities p_r depend on the random offspring counts. Lemmata and show that this probability converges to the correct limit. This completes the induction.

nodes.statement: Consider any xi in E consisting of k blocks (1leq kleq n-1), and any xi^primein E consisting of k+1 blocks. Setting eta=xi in , p_xixi(t) = frac1(N)_k sum_substacki_1,dots,i_k=1 \\ all distinct^N nu_t^(i_1) cdots nu_t^(i_k) . Similarly, p_xi^primexi^prime(t) &= frac1(N)_k+1 sum_substacki_1,dots, i_k+1 =1 \\ all distinct^N nu_t^(i_1) cdots nu_t^(i_k) nu_t^(i_k+1) \\ &= frac1(N)_k(N-k) sum_substacki_1,dots,i_k =1 \\ all distinct^N Bigg\ nu_t^(i_1) cdots nu_t^(i_k) sum_substacki_k+1=1 \\ notin \i_1,ldots, i_k\ ^N nu_t^(i_k+1) Bigg\ . Discarding the zero summands, p_xi^primexi^prime(t) = frac1(N)_k(N-k) sum_substacki_1,dots,i_k =1 \\ all distinct: \\ nu_t^(i_1),dots,nu_t^(i_k) > 0 ^N Bigg\ nu_t^(i_1) cdots nu_t^(i_k) sum_substacki_k+1=1 \\ notin \i_1,ldots, i_k\ ^N nu_t^(i_k+1) Bigg\ . The inner sum is sum_substacki_k+1=1 \\ notin \i_1,ldots, i_k\ ^N nu_t^(i_k+1) = Bigg\ sum_i=1^N nu_t^(i) - sum_iin\i_1,dots,i_k\ nu_t^(i) Bigg\ leq N - k , since nu_t^(i_1),dots,nu_t^(i_k) are all at least 1. Hence p_xi^primexi^prime(t) leq fracN-k(N)_k(N-k) sum_substacki_1,dots,i_k =1 \\ all distinct: \\ nu_t^(i_1),dots,nu_t^(i_k) > 0 ^N nu_t^(i_1) cdots nu_t^(i_k) = p_xixi(t) . Thus, p_xixi(t) is decreasing in the number of blocks of xi, and is therefore minimised by taking xi = Delta, which uniquely achieves the maximum n blocks. This choice in turn maximises 1-p_xixi(t), as required.

Since we are summing over all permutations of s_ 1 : l , the inner sum depends on I only through I:= |I|. We may therefore replace the sum over I subseteq [l] with a sum over the size I of the subset and a binomial coefficient counting the number of terms in which the subset is of size I: &sum_I subseteq [l] B^l-|I| sum_substack s_1, dots, s_l =1 \\ all distinct ^tau_N(t) Bigg( prod_iinI c_N(s_i) Bigg) Bigg( prod_jnotinI D_N(s_j) Bigg) notag\\ &= sum_substack s_1, dots, s_l =1 \\ all distinct ^tau_N(t) prod_j=1^l c_N(s_j) + sum_I=0^l-1 binomlI B^l-I sum_substack s_1, dots, s_l =1 \\ all distinct ^tau_N(t) Bigg( prod_i=1^I c_N(s_i) Bigg) Bigg( prod_j=I+1^l D_N(s_j) Bigg), where we have also separated out the I = l term. There is always at least one D_N factor in the second term on the right-hand side, so using Proposition~, Lemma , and the Binomial Theorem, we can write sum_I=0^l-1binomlI B^l-I &sum_substack s_1, dots, s_l =1 \\ all distinct ^tau_N(t) Bigg( prod_i=1^I c_N(s_i) Bigg) Bigg( prod_j=I+1^l D_N(s_j) Bigg) notag\\ &leq sum_I=0^l-1binomlI B^l-I Bigg( sum_substack s_1, dots, s_l-1 =1 \\ all distinct ^tau_N(t) prod_i=1^l-1 c_N(s_i) Bigg) sum_s_l=1^tau_N(t) D_N(s_l) notag\\ &leq sum_I=0^l-1binomlI B^l-I (t+1)^l-1 sum_s=1^tau_N(t) D_N(s) notag \\ &leq Bigg( sum_s=1^tau_N(t) D_N(s) Bigg) (t+1)^l-1 (1+B)^l. Substituting into concludes the proof.

Since our interest is the Ntoinfty limit, it is sufficient to have bounds that hold for large enough N. However, some of the manipulations to follow will also require pre-limiting bounds to be non-negative. For this reason we introduce indicator functions which guarantee non-negativity, but which will not affect the limit. The indicators introduced at this point are such that if their conditions do not hold then the bound becomes the trivial 1-p_r leq 1. When N geq 3, a sufficient condition to ensure that the expression on the right-hand side of is non-negative is that the event E_N^1(r) := left\ c_N(r) < alpha_n^-1 1_N right\ occurs, where the sequence 1_N is the same as that in . Bigg[ t^l - Bigg( sum_s=1^tau_N(t) c_N(s)^2 Bigg) binoml2(t+1)^l Bigg] - sum_substackl=1 \\ odd ^tau_N(t) alpha_n^l \\ &phantomgeq times 1_N frac1l! (t+1)^l notag\\ & - Bigg( sum_s=1^tau_N(t) c_N(s)^2 Bigg) sum_substackl=2 \\ even ^tau_N(t) alpha_n^l 1_N frac1l! binoml2(t+1)^l notag\\ & - Bigg( sum_s=1^tau_N(t) D_N(s) Bigg) sum_substackl=1 \\ odd ^tau_N(t) alpha_n^l 1_N frac1l! Now, taking the expectation and limit, and applying -- to show that all but the first sum vanish, and Lemmata and to show that lim_Ntoinfty P[ \tau_N(t) geq l\ cap E_N^3 ] =1, lim_Ntoinfty E Bigg[ prod_r=1^tau_N(t) (1-p_r) Bigg] &geq sum_l=0^infty (-alpha_n)^l 1_N frac1l! t^l lim_Ntoinfty Pleft[ \tau_N(t) geq l\ cap E_N^3 right] notag\\ & - lim_Ntoinfty E Bigg[ sum_s=1^tau_N(t) c_N(s)^2 Bigg] frac12 alpha_n^2 (t+1)^2 exp[ alpha_n (t+1) ]notag\\ & - lim_Ntoinfty E Bigg[ c_N(tau_N(t)) Bigg] exp[ alpha_n (t+1) ] notag\\ & - lim_Ntoinfty E Bigg[ sum_s=1^tau_N(t) D_N(s) Bigg] exp[ alpha_n (t+1) (1+B_n) ] notag\\ &= sum_l=0^infty (-alpha_n)^l frac1l! t^l = e^-alpha_n t. \begin{align}
\lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \prod_{r=1}^{\tau_N(t)} (1-p_r) \Bigg]
&\geq \sum_{l=0}^{\infty} (-\alpha_n)^l 1_N \frac{1}{l!} t^l 
        \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{P}\left[ \{\tau_N(t) \geq l\} \cap E_N^3 \right] \notag\\
    &\qquad- \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \sum_{s=1}^{\tau_N(t)} c_N(s)^2 \Bigg]
        \frac{1}{2} \alpha_n^2 (t+1)^2 \exp[ \alpha_n (t+1) ]\notag\\
    &\qquad- \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ c_N(\tau_N(t)) \Bigg] 
        \exp[ \alpha_n (t+1) ] \notag\\
    &\qquad- \lim_{N\to\infty} \mathbb{E} \Bigg[ \sum_{s=1}^{\tau_N(t)} D_N(s) \Bigg]
        \exp[ \alpha_n (t+1) (1+B_n) ] \notag\\
&= \sum_{l=0}^{\infty} (-\alpha_n)^l \frac{1}{l!} t^l
= e^{-\alpha_n t}. \label{eq:029}
\end{align}

For the last line of , recalling that D_N(t) leq c_N(t) (Proposition~), &- sum_l=1^tau_N(t) -k (-alpha_n)^l 1_N frac1l! sum_substacks_1, dots, s_l =1 \\ all distinct: \\ exists i,i^prime : s_i=r_i^prime ^tau_N(t) prod_j=1^l \ c_N(s_j) - B_n^prime D_N(s_j) \ \1E_N^1 cap E_N^2 \\ &leq sum_l=1^tau_N(t) -k alpha_n^l 1_N frac1l! sum_substacks_1, dots, s_l =1 \\ all distinct: \\ exists i,i^prime : s_i=r_i^prime ^tau_N(t) prod_j=1^l \ c_N(s_j) + B_n^prime D_N(s_j) \ \\ &leq sum_l=1^tau_N(t) -k alpha_n^l 1_N frac1l! sum_substacks_1, dots, s_l =1 \\ all distinct: \\ exists i,i^prime : s_i=r_i^prime ^tau_N(t) (1 + B_n^prime)^l prod_j=1^l c_N(s_j) \\ &leq sum_s in \r_1,dots,r_k\ c_N(s) sum_l=1^tau_N(t) -k alpha_n^l 1_N frac1(l-1)! (1 + B_n^prime)^l sum_substack s_1, dots, s_l-1 =1 \\ all distinct ^tau_N(t) prod_j=1^l-1 c_N(s_j) \\ &leq sum_j=1^k c_N(r_j) sum_l=1^tau_N(t) -k alpha_n^l 1_N frac1(l-1)! (1 + B_n^prime)^l (t+1)^l-1 \\ &leq left( sum_j=1^k c_N(r_j) right) alpha_n (1 + B_n^prime) exp[ alpha_n 1_N (1 + B_n^prime) (t+1) ] , where the penultimate inequality uses Lemma~. Substituting the preceding two displays into , we obtain prod_substackr=1 \\ notin \r_1,dots,r_k\ ^tau_N(t) (1-p_r)&leq 1+ sum_l=1^tau_N(t) -k (-alpha_n)^l 1_N frac1l! t^l \1E_N^1 cap E_N^2 + c_N(tau_N(t)) exp[ alpha_n 1_N (t+1) ] notag\\ & + left( sum_s=1^tau_N(t) c_N(s)^2 right) frac12 alpha_n^2 (t+1)^2 exp[ alpha_n 1_N (t+1) ] notag\\ & + left( sum_s=1^tau_N(t) D_N(s) right) exp[ alpha_n 1_N (t+1) (1+B_n^prime) ] notag\\ & + left( sum_j=1^k c_N(r_j) right) alpha_n (1 + B_n^prime) exp[ alpha_n 1_N (1 + B_n^prime) (t+1) ] . To obtain a corresponding bound for p_r, we use and Lemma~ (with ordered rather than distinct indices) to obtain sum_substackr_1 <dots< r_k :\\ r_i leq tau_N(t_i) forall i prod_i=1^k p_r_i &leq alpha_n^k 1_N sum_substackr_1 <dots< r_k :\\ r_i leq tau_N(t_i) forall i prod_i=1^k left[ c_N(r_i) + B_n D_N(r_i) right] notag\\ &leq alpha_n^k 1_N sum_substackr_1 <dots< r_k :\\ r_i leq tau_N(t_i) forall i prod_i=1^k c_N(r_i) notag \\ &phantomleq + Bigg( sum_s=1^tau_N(t) D_N(s) Bigg) alpha_n^k 1_N (t+1)^k-1 (1+B_n)^k . The following looser but simpler bound will also be useful: prod_i=1^k p_r_i leq alpha_n^k 1_N prod_i=1^k left[ c_N(r_i) + B_n D_N(r_i) right] &leq alpha_n^k 1_N prod_i=1^k c_N(r_i) (1 + B_n) notag\\ &leq alpha_n^k 1_N (1 + B_n)^k prod_i=1^k c_N(r_i). Using Lemma~, also leads to the deterministic bound sum_substackr_1 <dots< r_k :\\ r_i leq tau_N(t_i) forall i prod_i=1^k p_r_i &leq alpha_n^k 1_N (1 + B_n)^k frac1k! sum_r_1 neq dotsneq r_k^tau_N(t) prod_i=1^k c_N(r_i) notag\\ &leq alpha_n^k 1_N (1 + B_n)^k frac1k! (t+1)^k. All the ingredients for obtaining the bound in the statement of Lemma are now in place. First, by , &sum_substackr_1 <dots< r_k :\\ r_i leq tau_N(t_i) forall i Bigg( prod_i=1^k p_r_i Bigg) Bigg( prod_substackr=1 \\ notin \r_1,dots,r_k\ ^tau_N(t) (1-p_r) Bigg) \\ &leq Bigg\ 1+ sum_l=1^tau_N(t) -k (-alpha_n)^l 1_N frac1l! t^l \1E_N^1 cap E_N^2 Bigg\ sum_substackr_1 <dots< r_k :\\ r_i leq tau_N(t_i) forall i prod_i=1^k p_r_i \\ &phantomleq + Bigg\ c_N(tau_N(t)) exp[ alpha_n 1_N (t+1) ] \\ &phantomleq + Bigg\ + Bigg( sum_s=1^tau_N(t) c_N(s)^2 Bigg) frac12 alpha_n^2 (t+1)^2 exp[ alpha_n 1_N (t+1) ] \\ &phantomleq + Bigg\ + Bigg( sum_s=1^tau_N(t) D_N(s) Bigg) exp[ alpha_n 1_N (t+1) (1+B_n^prime) ] Bigg\ sum_substackr_1 <dots< r_k :\\ r_i leq tau_N(t_i) forall i prod_i=1^k p_r_i \\ &phantomleq + exp[ alpha_n 1_N (1 + B_n^prime) (t+1) ] alpha_n (1 + B_n^prime) sum_substackr_1 <dots< r_k :\\ r_i leq tau_N(t_i) forall i sum_j=1^k c_N(r_j) prod_i=1^k p_r_i . To further bound the right-hand side, we apply to the first term, to the second, and to the third, yielding &sum_substackr_1 <dots< r_k :\\ r_i leq tau_N(t_i) forall i Bigg( prod_i=1^k p_r_i Bigg) Bigg( prod_substackr=1 \\ notin \r_1,dots,r_k\ ^tau_N(t) (1-p_r) Bigg) \\ &leq alpha_n^k 1_N Bigg\ 1+ sum_l=1^tau_N(t) -k (-alpha_n)^l 1_N frac1l! t^l \1E_N^1 cap E_N^2 Bigg\ sum_substackr_1 <dots< r_k :\\ r_i leq tau_N(t_i) forall i prod_i=1^k c_N(r_i) \\ &phantomleq+ Bigg( sum_s=1^tau_N(t) D_N(s) Bigg) alpha_n^k 1_N (t+1)^k-1 (1+B_n)^k sum_l=0^tau_N(t) (alpha_n)^l 1_N frac1l! t^l \\ &phantomleq+ Bigg\ c_N(tau_N(t)) exp[ alpha_n 1_N (t+1) ] + Bigg( sum_s=1^tau_N(t) c_N(s)^2 Bigg) frac12 alpha_n^2 (t+1)^2 exp[ alpha_n 1_N (t+1) ] \\ &phantomleq + Bigg\+ Bigg( sum_s=1^tau_N(t) D_N(s) Bigg) exp[ alpha_n 1_N (t+1) (1+B_n^prime) ] Bigg\ alpha_n^k 1_N (1 + B_n)^k frac(t+1)^kk! \\ &phantomleq+ exp[ alpha_n (1 + B_n^prime) (t+1) ] alpha_n (1 + B_n^prime) alpha_n^k 1_N (1 + B_n)^k \\ &hspace6cmtimes sum_substackr_1 <dots< r_k :\\ r_i leq tau_N(t_i) forall i sum_j=1^k c_N(r_j) prod_i=1^k c_N(r_i) . Taking an expectation and letting N to infty, the second, third, fourth, and fifth lines on the right-hand side vanish by --, leaving &lim_Ntoinfty E Bigg[ sum_substackr_1 <dots< r_k :\\ r_i leq tau_N(t_i) forall i Bigg( prod_i=1^k p_r_i Bigg) Bigg( prod_substackr=1 \\ notin \r_1,dots,r_k\ ^tau_N(t) (1-p_r) Bigg) Bigg] notag \\ &leq alpha_n^k lim_Ntoinfty E Bigg[ sum_substackr_1 <dots< r_k :\\ r_i leq tau_N(t_i) forall i prod_i=1^k c_N(r_i) Bigg] notag\\ &phantomleq + alpha_n^k sum_l=1^infty (-alpha_n)^l frac1l! t^l lim_Ntoinfty E Bigg[ Itau_N(t)geq k+l \1E_N^1 cap E_N^2 sum_substackr_1 <dots< r_k :\\ r_i leq tau_N(t_i) forall i prod_i=1^k c_N(r_i) Bigg] notag\\ &phantomleq+ exp[ alpha_n (1 + B_n^prime) (t+1) ] alpha_n^k+1 (1 + B_n^prime) (1 + B_n)^k notag\\ &phantomleq + times lim_Ntoinfty E Bigg[ sum_substackr_1 <dots< r_k :\\ r_i leq tau_N(t_i) forall i sum_j=1^k c_N(r_j) prod_i=1^k c_N(r_i) Bigg] , where passing the limit and expectation inside the infinite sum is justified by Lemma~. To see that the last line vanishes, recall that 0 = t_0 leq t_1 leq ldots leq t_k leq t, whereupon sum_substackr_1 <dots< r_k :\\ r_i leq tau_N(t_i) forall i sum_j=1^k c_N(r_j) prod_i=1^k c_N(r_i) &leq frac1k! sum_substackr_1, dots, r_k \\ all distinct ^tau_N(t) sum_j=1^k c_N(r_j) prod_i=1^k c_N(r_i) \\ &leq frac1k! sum_j=1^k sum_s=1^tau_N(t) c_N(s)^2 sum_substackr_1, dots, r_k-1 \\ all distinct ^tau_N(t) prod_i=1^k-1 c_N(r_i) \\ &leq frac1(k-1)! sum_s=1^tau_N(t) c_N(s)^2 (t+1)^k-1, using Lemma~ for the final inequality.
